40	def _prepare_defaults(columns, normalizing=frozenset()):
41	    """Validate the optional target-typed ``default`` of each column.
42	
43	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the processed default
44	    (string defaults are trimmed; a string column opting into NFKC also
45	    has its default NFKC-normalized and re-trimmed). A malformed default
46	    is a configuration error naming the default value and output field,
47	    raised before the input is read; the caller's schema dicts are never
48	    mutated. A normalized string default that becomes blank is refused
49	    here so the later ``allowed_values`` membership check keeps using
50	    the final emitted text.
51	    """
52	    defaults = {}
53	    for column in columns:
54	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
55	        if "default" not in column:
56	            continue
57	        default = column["default"]
58	        if kind == "string":
59	            if not isinstance(default, str):
60	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a string")
61	            processed = default.strip()
62	            if not processed:
63	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not be blank")
64	            if name in normalizing:
65	                processed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", processed).strip()
66	                if not processed:
67	                    raise ValueError(
68	                        f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not normalize to blank")
69	            defaults[name] = processed
70	        elif kind == "integer":
71	            if isinstance(default, bool) or not isinstance(default, int):
72	                raise ValueError(
73	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
74	            defaults[name] = default
75	        else:
76	            if not isinstance(default, bool):
77	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a boolean")
78	            defaults[name] = default
79	    return defaults

82	def _enum_field_error(name, value, allowed):
83	    """Return the enum error for a converted value, or None when it is allowed.
84	
85	    Null is never checked: an empty optional without a default stays null
86	    and membership is decided after type conversion and empty handling.

89	    if values is not None and value is not None and value not in values:
90	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is not one of allowed_values {values!r}"

94	def _prepare_allowed_values(columns, defaults):
95	    """Validate the optional ``allowed_values`` list of each column.
96	
97	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh list holding the
98	    declared entries verbatim (strings are neither trimmed nor case
99	    folded). The attribute must be a non-empty list of target-typed
100	    values: strings for ``string`` columns, non-boolean integers for
101	    ``integer`` columns, booleans for ``boolean`` columns; null, arrays
102	    and objects are never valid entries, and repeated entries (value
103	    equality, verbatim for strings) are refused. A processed default
104	    outside the list is a configuration error even when no row needs it.
105	    Raises ValueError naming ``allowed_values`` and the output field
106	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
107	    """
108	    allowed = {}
109	    for column in columns:
110	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
111	        if "allowed_values" not in column:
112	            continue
113	        values = column["allowed_values"]
114	        if not isinstance(values, list) or not values:
115	            raise ValueError(
116	                f"column {name!r} allowed_values {values!r} must be a non-empty list")
117	        checked = []
118	        for entry in values:
119	            if kind == "string":
120	                if not isinstance(entry, str):
121	                    raise ValueError(
122	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} must be a string")
123	            elif kind == "integer":
124	                if isinstance(entry, bool) or not isinstance(entry, int):
125	                    raise ValueError(
126	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} "
127	                        "must be a non-boolean integer")
128	            elif not isinstance(entry, bool):
129	                raise ValueError(
130	                    f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} must be a boolean")
131	            if entry in checked:
132	                raise ValueError(
133	                    f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} is repeated")
134	            checked.append(entry)
135	        allowed[name] = checked
136	        if name in defaults and defaults[name] not in checked:
137	            raise ValueError(
138	                f"column {name!r} default {defaults[name]!r} is not one of "
139	                f"allowed_values {checked!r}")
140	    return allowed

143	def _prepare_ranges(columns, defaults):
144	    """Validate the optional ``minimum``/``maximum`` bounds of each column.
145	
146	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a ``(minimum, maximum)``
147	    pair, with None for an unset end; either end may be declared alone
148	    and equal ends accept exactly that one integer. Bounds may appear
149	    only on ``integer`` columns and each must be a non-boolean integer
150	    (negative values and zero are legal): null, strings, floats and
151	    booleans are configuration errors, as is a minimum greater than the
152	    maximum. A processed default outside the declared range is a
153	    configuration error even when no row needs it. Raises ValueError
154	    naming the output field, the attribute and the offending value
155	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
156	    """
157	    ranges = {}
158	    for column in columns:
159	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
160	        bounds = {}
161	        for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
162	            if attribute not in column:
163	                continue
164	            bound = column[attribute]
165	            if kind != "integer":
166	                raise ValueError(
167	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} requires an integer column")
168	            if isinstance(bound, bool) or not isinstance(bound, int):
169	                raise ValueError(
170	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
171	            bounds[attribute] = bound
172	        if not bounds:
173	            continue
174	        minimum = bounds.get("minimum")
175	        maximum = bounds.get("maximum")
176	        if minimum is not None and maximum is not None and minimum > maximum:
177	            raise ValueError(
178	                f"column {name!r} minimum {minimum!r} is greater than "
179	                f"maximum {maximum!r}")
180	        if name in defaults:
181	            default = defaults[name]
182	            if minimum is not None and default < minimum:
183	                raise ValueError(
184	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is less than "
185	                    f"minimum {minimum!r}")
186	            if maximum is not None and default > maximum:
187	                raise ValueError(
188	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is greater than "
189	                    f"maximum {maximum!r}")
190	        ranges[name] = (minimum, maximum)
191	    return ranges

194	def _range_field_error(name, value, ranges):
195	    """Return the range error for a converted value, or None when in range.
196	
197	    Null is never checked: an empty optional without a default stays null
198	    and the inclusive bounds only see non-null integers, after type
199	    conversion, empty handling and the enum check.
200	    """
201	    bounds = ranges.get(name)
202	    if bounds is None or value is None:
203	        return None
204	    minimum, maximum = bounds
205	    if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
206	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is less than minimum {minimum!r}"
207	    if maximum is not None and value > maximum:
208	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is greater than maximum {maximum!r}"
209	    return None

212	def _lte_field_errors(record, field_errors, lte_fields):
213	    """Check every declared ``lte_field`` relation over final integers.
214	
215	    Runs after structure checks, marker matching, default filling, type
216	    conversion, enum and range checks. A relation is skipped when either
217	    final value is null or either participating field already has a
218	    required, type, enum or range error; the original errors are kept and
219	    every other relation is still checked. Relations are evaluated in
220	    schema column order and returned as ``(name, message)`` pairs so the
221	    caller can file each error under its declaring column's position; a
222	    violation names ``lte_field``, both output names and the two actual
223	    integers (the local value larger than the target value fails;
224	    equality is legal).
225	    """
226	    errors = []
227	    for name, target in lte_fields:
228	        if name in field_errors or target in field_errors:
229	            continue
230	        local = record.get(name)
231	        other = record.get(target)
232	        if local is None or other is None:
233	            continue
234	        if local > other:
235	            errors.append((
236	                name,
237	                f"{name}: value {local!r} is greater than lte_field "
238	                f"{target!r} value {other!r}"))
239	    return errors

242	def _prepare_lte_fields(columns):
243	    """Validate the optional ``lte_field`` reference of each integer column.
244	
245	    Returns a list of ``(name, target)`` pairs in schema column order, one
246	    entry per declaring column. The attribute must be a non-blank string
247	    naming another ``integer`` column by its output name (source aliases
248	    are not recognized); a non-string, a blank string, an unknown field,
249	    a self reference, a non-integer target, or declaring ``lte_field`` on
250	    a non-integer column is a configuration error. Raises ValueError
251	    naming ``lte_field``, the output field and the attribute value before
252	    the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
253	    """
254	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
255	    lte_fields = []
256	    for column in columns:
257	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
258	        if "lte_field" not in column:
259	            continue
260	        target = column["lte_field"]
261	        if not isinstance(target, str):
262	            raise ValueError(
263	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must be a string naming "
264	                "an integer column")
265	        if not target.strip():
266	            raise ValueError(
267	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must be a non-blank string")
268	        if kind != "integer":
269	            raise ValueError(
270	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} requires an integer column")
271	        if target == name:
272	            raise ValueError(
273	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must not reference the column itself")
274	        if target not in by_name:
275	            raise ValueError(
276	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} is not a schema column name")
277	        if by_name[target]["type"] != "integer":
278	            raise ValueError(
279	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must reference an integer column")
280	        lte_fields.append((name, target))
281	    return lte_fields

321	def _prepare_boolean_aliases(columns):
322	    """Validate the optional ``boolean_aliases`` mapping of each boolean column.
323	
324	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh dict keyed by the
325	    normalized alias text (the declared key trimmed and Unicode
326	    casefolded) holding the target boolean verbatim. The attribute must be
327	    a non-empty object and may appear only on a ``boolean`` column; every
328	    key must be a non-blank string and every mapped value a boolean. Two
329	    keys that normalize to the same text are invalid even when they map to
330	    the same boolean, and a key normalizing to ``true`` or ``false`` is
331	    refused so the built-in spellings keep their fixed meaning. Raises
332	    ValueError naming ``boolean_aliases``, the output field and the
333	    offending value before the input is read; the caller's schema is never
334	    mutated.
335	    """
336	    aliases = {}
337	    for column in columns:
338	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
339	        if "boolean_aliases" not in column:
340	            continue
341	        configured = column["boolean_aliases"]
342	        if kind != "boolean":
343	            raise ValueError(
344	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} requires a boolean column")
345	        if not isinstance(configured, dict) or not configured:
346	            raise ValueError(
347	                f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases {configured!r} must be a non-empty object")
348	        normalized = {}
349	        for key, mapped in configured.items():
350	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
351	                raise ValueError(
352	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} must be a non-blank string")
353	            if not isinstance(mapped, bool):
354	                raise ValueError(
355	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases value {mapped!r} for key {key!r} "
356	                    "must be a boolean")
357	            folded = key.strip().casefold()
358	            if folded in ("true", "false"):
359	                raise ValueError(
360	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} must not normalize to "
361	                    f"the built-in boolean spelling {folded!r}")
362	            if folded in normalized:
363	                raise ValueError(
364	                    f"column {name!r} boolean_aliases key {key!r} normalizes to a repeated "
365	                    f"key {folded!r}")
366	            normalized[folded] = mapped
367	        aliases[name] = normalized

371	def _validate_schema_structure(schema):
372	    """Validate the structural shape of the schema before any file is read.
373	
374	    The schema must be an object holding a non-empty ``columns`` list;
375	    each column must be an object carrying ``name`` (a non-blank string,
376	    kept verbatim -- never trimmed -- and unique case-sensitively) and
377	    ``type`` (one of ``string``, ``integer``, ``boolean``), plus an
378	    optional ``required`` that, when present, must be a boolean. Checks
379	    run top level first, then column by column in order (column
380	    structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first
381	    problem is reported: the ValueError message names ``schema`` and the
382	    one-based column position, names a missing key, carries the
383	    offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later
384	    column. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema is
385	    never mutated.
386	    """
387	    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
388	        raise ValueError(f"schema must be an object, got {schema!r}")
389	    if "columns" not in schema:
390	        raise ValueError("schema is missing 'columns'")
391	    columns = schema["columns"]
392	    if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
393	        raise ValueError(f"schema 'columns' must be a non-empty list, got {columns!r}")
394	    seen = {}

448	def _prepare_field_list(fields, names, option):
449	    """Validate a list option of output field names shared by the two
450	    report/dedup features.
451	
452	    Returns a new list (the caller's list is never mutated or retained)
453	    or None when the option is disabled. The value must be a non-empty
454	    list of non-blank strings naming schema output columns literally
455	    (names are neither trimmed nor case folded, and source aliases are
456	    not recognized); a non-list, an empty list, a non-string or blank
457	    entry, a repeat, or an unknown field raises ValueError naming the
458	    option and the offending value before the input is read.
459	    """
460	    if fields is None:
461	        return None
462	    if not isinstance(fields, list):
463	        raise ValueError(f"{option} must be a list of schema field names")
464	    if not fields:
465	        raise ValueError(f"{option} must not be empty")
466	    known = set(names)
467	    seen = set()
468	    for member in fields:
469	        if not isinstance(member, str) or not member.strip():
470	            raise ValueError(f"{option} entry {member!r} must be a non-blank string")
471	        if member in seen:
472	            raise ValueError(f"{option} field {member!r} is repeated")
473	        if member not in known:
474	            raise ValueError(f"{option} field {member!r} is not a schema column name")
475	        seen.add(member)
476	    return list(fields)

506	    """Group accepted records by the converted values of duplicate_by fields."""
507	    groups = {}

518	def _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns):
519	    """Validate the optional single-field equality filter.
520	
521	    The condition is an object with exactly ``field`` and ``value`` keys;
522	    field matches an output name literally (source aliases are not
523	    recognized) and value must fit the target type, with null allowed for
524	    every type. Returns (field, value) or None when filtering is disabled.
525	    Raises ValueError before the input is read.
526	    """
527	    if filter_eq is None:
528	        return None
529	    if not isinstance(filter_eq, dict):
530	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must be an object with 'field' and 'value' keys")
531	    keys = set(filter_eq)
532	    if keys != {"field", "value"}:
533	        details = []
534	        missing = [key for key in ("field", "value") if key not in keys]
535	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "value"})
536	        if missing:
537	            details.append("missing key(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
538	        if extra:
539	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))
540	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must contain exactly 'field' and 'value' keys (" + "; ".join(details) + ")")
541	    field = filter_eq["field"]
542	    if not isinstance(field, str):
543	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a string")
544	    if not field.strip():
545	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a non-blank string")
546	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
547	    if field not in by_name:
548	        raise ValueError(f"filter_eq field {field!r} is not a schema column name")
549	    value = filter_eq["value"]
550	    kind = by_name[field]["type"]
551	    if value is not None:
552	        if kind == "string" and not isinstance(value, str):
553	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a string or null")
554	        if kind == "integer" and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int)):
555	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a non-boolean integer or null")
556	        if kind == "boolean" and not isinstance(value, bool):
557	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a boolean or null")
558	    return field, value

561	def _deduplicate_records(records, deduplicate_by):
562	    """Keep the first record of each equal-key group, in input order.
563	
564	    Two records collide only when every named field's final value is
565	    equal (strings case-sensitively, null equal to null). The first
566	    record in input order is kept complete -- non-key fields are never
567	    merged or overwritten -- and the remaining records keep their
568	    relative order. Returns (kept, removed_count).
569	    """
570	    seen_keys = set()
571	    kept = []
572	    for record in records:
573	        key = tuple(record[field] for field in deduplicate_by)
574	        if key in seen_keys:
575	            continue
576	        seen_keys.add(key)
577	        kept.append(record)
578	    return kept, len(records) - len(kept)

581	def _build_result(records, errors, duplicate_fields, filter_condition,
582	                  deduplicate_fields=None):
583	    """Filter fully validated records, then keep-first dedup, then counts.
584	
585	    Order is: validation (already done by the caller), ``filter_eq``,
586	    keep-first deduplication over the filter survivors, and finally the
587	    duplicate report over the records that remain.
588	    """
589	    if filter_condition is None:
590	        filtered_records, filtered_count = records, 0
591	    else:
592	        field, expected = filter_condition
593	        filtered_records = [record for record in records if record[field] == expected]
594	        filtered_count = len(records) - len(filtered_records)
595	    if deduplicate_fields is None:
596	        kept, deduplicated_count = filtered_records, 0
597	    else:
598	        kept, deduplicated_count = _deduplicate_records(
599	            filtered_records, deduplicate_fields)
600	    result = {"records": kept, "errors": errors, "accepted": len(kept),
601	              "rejected": len(errors)}
602	    if filter_condition is not None:
603	        result["filtered"] = filtered_count
604	    if deduplicate_fields is not None:
605	        result["deduplicated"] = deduplicated_count
606	    if duplicate_fields is not None:
607	        result["duplicates"] = _find_duplicates(kept, duplicate_fields)
608	    return result

611	def _csv_parse_error(source, start_line, reason):
612	    """Build the ValueError for a fatal CSV quote-syntax failure.
613	
614	    The message carries the literal "CSV parse error", the input path, the
615	    offending record's starting physical line (header is line 1; a data
616	    record starts on the physical line after the preceding row ends), and
617	    a reason distinguishing a quote left open at end of file from text
618	    appearing right after a closing quote.
619	    """
620	    return ValueError(
621	        f"CSV parse error in {source} at record starting line {start_line}: {reason}")

624	def _csv_error_reason(exc):
625	    """Map a strict-reader ``csv.Error`` onto the two fatal quote problems.
626	
627	    ``strict=True`` raises "unexpected end of data" for a quoted field
628	    still open at EOF and "',' expected after '\"'" for any character
629	    other than comma/newline/EOF right after a closing quote (spaces and
630	    tabs included). Anything else is reported verbatim.
631	    """
632	    message = str(exc)
633	    if message == "unexpected end of data":
634	        return ("unterminated quoted field: a double-quoted field was still "
635	                "open when the file ended")
636	    if "expected after" in message:
637	        return ("invalid text after closing quote: only a comma, a line "
638	                "ending or the end of the file may follow a closing "
639	                "double quote")
640	    return message

643	def _nfkc(value):
644	    """NFKC-normalize an already trimmed string and trim it again.
645	
646	    Compatibility composition folds full-width letters onto ASCII and
647	    merges combining-mark sequences (``e`` + U+0301 -> ``é``); NFKC may
648	    leave fresh leading/trailing whitespace (full-width space U+3000
649	    becomes an ASCII space), so the result is trimmed once more.
650	    """
651	    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).strip()

654	def normalize_csv(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None,
655	                  deduplicate_by=None):
656	    columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers, aliases, ranges, lte_fields, normalizing = _prepare_schema(schema)
657	    names = [column["name"] for column in columns]
658	    column_index = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(names)}
659	    duplicate_fields = _prepare_duplicate_by(duplicate_by, names)
660	    deduplicate_fields = _prepare_deduplicate_by(deduplicate_by, names)
661	    filter_condition = _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns)
662	    records, errors = [], []
663	    # strict=True turns the two quote-syntax problems that a lenient reader
664	    # silently folds into the data into csv.Error: a quoted field still open
665	    # at EOF and any character other than comma/newline/EOF right after a
666	    # closing quote (a space or tab included). A doubled "" inside a quoted
667	    # field still decodes to one literal double quote, and a double quote
668	    # inside an unquoted field stays an ordinary character.
669	    with Path(source).open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
670	        reader = csv.reader(handle, strict=True)
671	        # reader.line_num is the physical line where the row just read ends;
672	        # LF, CRLF (counted once) and a lone CR all terminate a line. A
673	        # record's starting physical line is one past the end of the
674	        # preceding row, so skipped empty lines and newlines inside quoted
675	        # fields shift it down. When the strict reader reports a syntax
676	        # error the failing record starts on previous_end + 1, even though
677	        # the problem is only detected at a later physical line or at EOF.
678	        previous_end = 0
679	        header = None
680	        try:
681	            for cells in reader:
682	                start_line = previous_end + 1
683	                previous_end = reader.line_num
684	                if header is None:
685	                    header = cells
686	                    if header != sources:
687	                        raise ValueError(
688	                            "CSV header must match schema column sources and order exactly")
689	                    continue
690	                if not cells:
691	                    # An ordinary empty physical line: skipped as a record but it
692	                    # still occupies a physical line number (tracked above).
693	                    continue
694	                record = {}
695	                if len(cells) != len(sources):
696	                    row_errors = ["wrong number of cells"]
697	                else:
698	                    # One error slot per column keeps per-field errors and
699	                    # the lte_field relation error attributed to a column in
700	                    # schema column order, even when the relation points
701	                    # backward at an earlier column.
702	                    slots = [[] for _ in columns]
703	                    field_error_names = set()
704	                    for index, (column, value) in enumerate(zip(columns, cells)):
705	                        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
706	                        value = value.strip()
707	                        if value in markers.get(name, ()):
708	                            # A declared missing marker matches the trimmed
709	                            # cell exactly (case-sensitive) before any type
710	                            # conversion and then follows the empty-value
711	                            # flow: default, required error or null.
712	                            value = ""
713	                        try:
714	                            if not value:
715	                                if name in defaults:
716	                                    converted = defaults[name]
717	                                elif column.get("required", False):
718	                                    raise ValueError("required value is empty")
719	                                else:
720	                                    converted = None
721	                            elif kind == "integer":
722	                                converted = int(value)
723	                            elif kind == "boolean":
724	                                folded = value.casefold()
725	                                if folded in ("true", "false"):
726	                                    converted = folded == "true"
727	                                elif folded in aliases.get(name, ()):
728	                                    converted = aliases[name][folded]
729	                                else:
730	                                    raise ValueError("boolean must be true or false")
731	                            else:
732	                                converted = value
733	                                if name in normalizing:
734	                                    converted = _nfkc(converted)
735	                                    if not converted:
736	                                        # A non-empty trimmed value whose
737	                                        # NFKC normalization collapses to
738	                                        # blank follows the ordinary
739	                                        # empty-value flow; markers are not
740	                                        # matched a second time and a filled
741	                                        # default was normalized at load.
742	                                        if name in defaults:
743	                                            converted = defaults[name]
744	                                        elif column.get("required", False):
745	                                            raise ValueError("required value is empty")
746	                                        else:
747	                                            converted = None
748	                        except ValueError as exc:
749	                            slots[index].append(f"{name}: {exc}")
750	                            field_error_names.add(name)
751	                            continue
752	                        enum_error = _enum_field_error(name, converted, allowed)
753	                        if enum_error is not None:
754	                            slots[index].append(enum_error)
755	                            field_error_names.add(name)
756	                            continue
757	                        range_error = _range_field_error(name, converted, ranges)
758	                        if range_error is not None:
759	                            slots[index].append(range_error)
760	                            field_error_names.add(name)
761	                        else:
762	                            record[name] = converted
763	                    for name, message in _lte_field_errors(
764	                            record, field_error_names, lte_fields):
765	                        slots[column_index[name]].append(message)
766	                    row_errors = [message for slot in slots for message in slot]
767	                if row_errors:
768	                    errors.append({"row": start_line, "errors": row_errors})
769	                else:
770	                    records.append(record)
771	        except csv.Error as exc:
772	            raise _csv_parse_error(
773	                source, previous_end + 1, _csv_error_reason(exc)) from None
774	        if header is None:
775	            raise ValueError("CSV header must match schema column sources and order exactly")
776	    return _build_result(records, errors, duplicate_fields, filter_condition,
777	                         deduplicate_fields)

780	def _convert_jsonl_value(column, value, defaults, markers, aliases,
781	                         normalizing=frozenset()):
782	    """Convert one decoded JSON value. Returns (converted, error_message)."""
783	    name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
784	    if isinstance(value, str):
785	        value = value.strip()
786	        if value in markers.get(name, ()):
787	            # Only JSON strings take part in marker matching (numbers,
788	            # booleans, arrays and objects never do); a hit follows the
789	            # empty-value flow before any type conversion.
790	            value = ""
791	    if value is None or value == "":
792	        if name in defaults:
793	            return defaults[name], None
794	        if column.get("required", False):
795	            return None, f"{name}: required value is empty"
796	        return None, None
797	    if kind == "string":
798	        if not isinstance(value, str):
799	            return None, f"{name}: expected string"
800	        if name in normalizing:
801	            normalized = _nfkc(value)
802	            if not normalized:
803	                # NFKC collapsed a non-empty string to blank: the ordinary
804	                # empty-value flow applies, without matching markers again;
805	                # a filled default was normalized at load.
806	                if name in defaults:
807	                    return defaults[name], None
808	                if column.get("required", False):
809	                    return None, f"{name}: required value is empty"
810	                return None, None
811	            value = normalized
812	        return value, None
813	    if kind == "integer":
814	        if isinstance(value, bool):
815	            return None, f"{name}: expected integer"
816	        if isinstance(value, int):
817	            return value, None
818	        if isinstance(value, str):
819	            try:
820	                return int(value), None
821	            except ValueError:
822	                pass
823	        return None, f"{name}: expected integer"
824	    if isinstance(value, bool):
825	        return value, None
826	    if isinstance(value, str):
827	        folded = value.casefold()
828	        if folded in ("true", "false"):
829	            return folded == "true", None
830	        column_aliases = aliases.get(name)
831	        if column_aliases is not None and folded in column_aliases:
832	            return column_aliases[folded], None
833	    return None, f"{name}: boolean must be true or false"

929	def _csv_cell(value, quote_empty=False):
930	    """Serialize one normalized value to a single CSV cell.
931	
932	    Integers are decimal text (booleans, checked first, are lowercase
933	    ``true``/``false``), null is an empty cell, and strings keep their
934	    normalized content including any embedded CR/LF characters. The same
935	    quoting rule applies to every cell (headers included): a cell that
936	    contains a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes
937	    with each interior double quote doubled. An empty cell stays bare,
938	    except in a single-column table (``quote_empty``), where it must be a
939	    quoted empty string so the row cannot collapse into a skipped blank
940	    line; every other cell stays unquoted.
